newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: U.S. blocks early WTO panel on Cuba trade law.
newsitem.headline: U.S. blocks early WTO panel on Cuba trade law.

text.p: The United States on Wednesday refused to agree to quick creation of a panel requested by the European Union to determine whether the Helms-Burton law on investment in Cuba fitted global free trade rules.
Booth Gardner, U.S. ambassador to the World Trade Organisation (WTO), appealed to the EU to reconsider its request, arguing that the case was a political question and not a trade issue, they added.

But a neutral panel on the Helms-Burton dispute will be created automatically at the next regular meeting of the DSB, scheduled for November 20 -- three weeks after the U.S. election. A member state may only refuse once to set up a panel.

Ian Wilkinson, acting head of the EU delegation in Geneva, requested the panel at the closed-door DSB. In a statement he said the Community objected "to the U.S. trying to force other countries to follow their own foreign policy objectives through the threat and actual imposition of trade sanctions".
The Community also objected to Washington "exerting jurisdiction" over U.S.-controlled companies registered in the European Community member states, according to the EU envoy.

Cuba's trade ambassador Eumelio Caballero told the DSB that the U.S. law violated WTO free trade agreements because they were unilateral and extraterritorial. In a text distributed by Cuban officials, he said the Helms-Burton law and other U.S. measures against Havana "violate the rights of both my country and other member states of the WTO".
